note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a venue has, what it costs, whether it is lit - come from the Town of Mount Pleasant and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Charleston County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the first county in South Carolina this directory has published in, and one town of it is on this page.

slots.coverage: One municipality in Charleston County is published here: Mount Pleasant, with four venues and nineteen courts verified against the Town of Mount Pleasant's own pickleball page. The City of Charleston was read and refused: its pickleball page names parks without stating a court count for any of them, and a venue with no stated count does not publish, whatever it plainly has. North Charleston has not been read, and neither have Charleston County's own parks, so neither appears here in any form - not as refused, not as pending, simply unread. The same is true of every other municipality in the county. What this page reports, then, is one town's inventory and nothing wider: ten courts at Park West, four at The Deb Gym at Town Hall, four at Miriam Brown Community Center and one at the Mount Pleasant Senior Center, every one of them with a count, an address and a paragraph of rules on a single Town page, and every address matched at house-number level by the US Census geocoder to Charleston County and to the incorporated place Mount Pleasant town. Nothing in Mount Pleasant was refused. That is a fact about the Town's page rather than about the town: it prints a count under every entry, which the City of Charleston does not, and that single habit is the whole difference between the two on this site.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county sits in one town, and within it the split that matters is indoor against outdoor rather than north against south. Eleven of the nineteen courts are in gymnasiums - six at Park West Gym, four at the Deb Gym at Town Hall, one at the Senior Center - and exist at scheduled session times, when the Town's nets go up on a floor it also uses for basketball, badminton and, at the Deb Gym each autumn, volleyball. Eight are outdoors: four on the Park West tennis courts and four at Miriam Brown Community Center. Park West is the one site with courts on both sides of the line, ten at a single address, and it is also where the county's only stated lighting is, "4 Courts - Lighted", on the tennis courts. So of nineteen courts, four are lit, four outdoors carry no lighting answer, and eleven are indoors where the question does not arise. Free play follows the same shape: eighteen of the nineteen courts are free in the Town's words, and the one that is not is the Senior Center's single court, free for members and a $5 or $10 guest fee otherwise, for players 50 and older. The hours divide the same way. The gyms and the Senior Center run on weekday daytimes; the Park West tennis courts carry the Town's evening group, Monday to Wednesday, 6:00 to 8:00 pm; Miriam Brown carries the one daily session, mornings 7:00 to 11:00, and a printed afternoon ban. Nothing here is a destination complex, and the largest single count in the county is Park West's six-court gym.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a Mount Pleasant page under the heading of a county in which the City of Charleston has been read and refused, and the other parks departments have not been read at all. The City of Charleston is the biggest gap and the most frustrating one, because it is not a silence: its pickleball page names parks. It does not say how many courts any of them has, and a name without a count is not enough for a venue page here. If the City adds a number under each park, that page can be read again. North Charleston has not been opened. The County's own parks have not been opened either, and nothing on this page should be taken as a statement about what either holds. Inside Mount Pleasant the gaps are of a different kind, and they are all silences rather than refusals. The Town states no surface for any court. It states lighting for the Park West tennis courts and nothing about Miriam Brown's four outdoor courts, so those are recorded as unverified rather than assumed unlit. It states no parking, no restrooms and no building hours on its pickleball page - the times published here are pickleball sessions - and nothing about how busy any session gets. Nothing outside a municipal recreation department appears on this page at all. Clubs, private facilities and any courts in the county's residential communities publish no source this site could read, so none is listed, and that absence is about who writes things down rather than about where the game is played.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Charleston County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and this page does not pretend to. What we have checked is 19 courts across four venues, all in Mount Pleasant, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Charleston names pickleball parks without counting their courts, and North Charleston and the County's own parks have not been read.

faqs.q: Why is only Mount Pleasant listed?
faqs.a: Because it is the one municipality in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A town appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source and a date. The City of Charleston was read and refused for stating no counts; North Charleston and the County's parks have not been read.

faqs.q: Why is the City of Charleston not listed?
faqs.a: Its pickleball page names parks without stating how many courts each has, and a venue without a stated count does not publish here. That is a refusal on the record rather than a gap in reading; if the City adds counts under its parks, the page will be read again.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Eighteen of the nineteen are, in the Town's words: "Drop-in play is free" under the two gyms, and "free and first come, first served" at Miriam Brown and on the Park West tennis courts. The Senior Center's one court is free for members and a $5 or $10 guest fee otherwise, for players 50 and older.

The four Park West tennis courts, which the Town lists as "4 Courts - Lighted". Miriam Brown's four outdoor courts carry no lighting statement either way, so they are recorded as unverified rather than as unlit. The eleven indoor courts are in gyms, where the Town does not address the question.

faqs.q: Where can I play indoors in Charleston County?
faqs.a: In Mount Pleasant, at three gyms: Park West Gym with six courts, The Deb Gym at Town Hall with four and the Senior Center with one, all at session times the Town prints. Between them that is eleven indoor courts, more than the county's verified outdoor eight. No other municipality has been read.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and the Town's page is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If the Town changes a count, drops the volleyball-season note at the Deb Gym or adds a lighting line at Miriam Brown, the build fails and someone reads the page again.
